cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: New players face immediate friction from severe toxicity, frustrating balance, and disruptive audio cues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the community exhibits extreme toxicity and a tribalistic us-versus-them mindset.

citations.review_text:
1.4k hours on console.

Really great concepts love the asym nature, hate the 'balancing'. People want this game balanced and the devs balance it 60/40 but in this balancing they make it extremely unfun. I play both sides and genuinely every perk update its just more micro optimization. I wish the devs could just give fun metas on both sides that aren't op. 

Current killer design is really bad and heavily recycled. Since the lich and drac I don't think we've really got a unique power which is a shame. 

And I will say the community in this game is hit or miss. I've had great interactions and much more really disgusting awful interactions. Not to say the game is bad for its playerbase but it cultivated a us vs them tribalistic mindset and as someone who pretty evenly plays both sides it makes the game very unbearable. 

After a long day the last thing I wanna do is open this game and for a game that's asymmetrical in design I think the fact they do so much power creep and unfun design on both sides it makes this not enjoyable. At the highest macro level game you're rotting your mind. Micro game good, everything surrounding it is very meh. 

I'd only play this with friends very unseriously unless they overhaul the whole game.

Dead by Daylight is one of the most frustrating games I've ever played. Every match feels like a coin flip where skill matters far less than bad matchmaking and random luck. The balance is constantly all over the place, with some killers or survivor perks making games feel completely miserable. Instead of having fun, I spend most of my time getting tunneled, camped, or matched against players far above my level. The servers seem to have a talent for giving hits that make absolutely no sense. Grinding for characters and perks takes forever, making the progression feel more like a second job than a game. Bugs somehow survive every update, while new ones appear just as often. The community can be unbelievably toxic, turning almost every match into a contest of who can be the most annoying. Even when I win, I usually feel relieved that it's over rather than excited. Dead by Daylight has a fantastic concept, but the actual experience is so infuriating that it's hard to recommend to anyone looking to have fun.

I had fun for an hour, watched content and saw the amount of toxic people going out of their way to ruin people lives in and out of game. Im scared to even try this game now. I dont understand why the Company doesnt punish people and turns a blind eye to these bullys. Im not gonna invest myself into a potential life risk.

I had this game on my wishlist for a while as a huge lover of asymmetrical horror! One of my friends ended up gifting me it for my birthday a few years back and I never got around to playing until recently! 

From the tutorial the game seemed great, good mechanics and brilliant graphics. I liked the diverse characters. 

However, I have autism, and I'm very sensitive to loud noises/sounds. And what the tutorial doesn't show you is that after just one hit from the killer your survivor will be none stop shrieking, grunting and sobbing. It is so loud, and extremely overstimulating. 

There is no way to counter this, the game volume is not separated, and muting it will mute the entire game. Even with heartbeat visualizer on, I still need audio cues for generators.  The game became unplayable after one regular match. 

You can not mod it to mute the survivors either, as any form of mod triggers the eac and risks getting you permanently banned.  Apparently from googling this issue, people have been asking for a feature to mute / turn down survivors for three years now.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that players can get stuck on janky geometry while trying to run around the map.

citations.review_text:
I've put over a hundred hours between this and console and I can honestly say do I recommend it? Maybe. 

Gameplay: 
You play as either one of the survivors or the killer. As a survivor your goal is to repair 5 generators and escape from the exit gate with your team. As the killer it is your job to stop them by either killing them or sacrificing them to the entity using hooks placed around the maps. The core game play loop is good, and its fun. 

As you level up either side you get  a currency called blood-points which can be used to level your characters in order to obtain new perks (i.e perks that help you distract the killer so your team can do generators, perks to heal faster, do generators faster, or hide better from the killer). 

as a killer you gain perks to slow down generator repair, kill survivors faster or read "aura's" (think of it as wall hacks for a short amount of time). 

Overall the gameplay loop is fun. 

DIFFICULTIES: 
- the game is kind of buggy, sometimes as a survivor or as a killer you will get stuck on janky pieces of geometry while trying to run around. Especially during certain events. 

- There is a META, but don't let that stop you from trying new builds, do what is fun, not what is the best. A game is meant to be fun, once you stop having fun just take a break from it. 

- Killers and survivors can be toxic. This is why I enjoy playing on console more than PC. There is a pre-game and end-game chat and if either side doesn't perform super well some people are just butt holes about the whole thing. Unfortunately you'll find that in ANY multiplayer game where there is some competition. 

- Some of the Survivors, Killers and cosmetics are locked behind paying for them due to their licensing agreements. Which means short of waiting for the perks to show up in a weekly "Shrine of secrets" which you can use a currency called Iridecent shards to unlock, to get their perks you would need to buy that character. This currency isn…

Will not be wasting more hours on this product, but..
[h1]No, absolutely NOT. Stay away from this game.[/h1]

This game makes you think even starting a new Terraria with Legendary difficulty is a more sane idea, instead of whatever "hockey" game this is.

The 20$SG price is a lie. The devs are incredibly scummy and predatory with how the whole "DLC" actually is about ~80$ and IT IS pay-2-win due to some perks don't and catered to the lower denominator who don't have the interest to get better at the game. See: This 10th anniv. event.

[h2]Main Complaints[/h2]
I'm surprised the game lasted for this long despite literally having no gameplay besides pressing [E] and aiming for skill checks. Is there really any transferrable skill there? Players would leave for the slightest offense, even though the role is literally boring.

Playing killer too, is horrible because once again - the P2W DLC perks gives surv so many second chances for FREE, which both the devs and the average players tried to vehemently defend to no end.

[h2]Off-Note[/h2]
I don't think I need to really discuss anything having to do with the community trying to enforce some kind of rulebook here; since having to read a wiki for 200+ perks is already a steep ravine to climb. Not to mention the terrible hitboxes and various "surprise mechanics" such as overpriced reskins (that actually gives you advantages by i.e. making no noises) to keep you hooked.

Anyways, Practice MENTAL GYMNASTICS in real time on Twitter or something. Seriously.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that playing as a killer can feel stressful and overwhelming when facing coordinated groups of survivors.

citations.review_text: this game is a wakeup call to killer mains whenever they match 4 stack of survivors who know every single maps pallet spawn locations and play like their family is being held at gunpoint and the criteria for their release is to make the killer take the lives of their entire family with a shotgun and them to turn it on themselves

It is, without a doubt, an incredible game. I’ve been playing it for a long time and its formula remains one of the most fun and addictive within the asymmetrical horror genre. Every match gives you unique moments of tension, and it's one of those games where hours just fly by.

However, I believe the development team seriously needs to balance the matches more, especially on the killer side. Playing as a killer nowadays has become extremely frustrating; you suffer way too much at high ranks. Between the tremendous speed at which generators are repaired and the incredible coordination that survivor groups can have through communication, the pressure on the killer is overwhelming. I feel the scale is heavily tipped in favor of the survivors, and an adjustment is necessary so that the killer role can be enjoyable again rather than a stressful experience.

On the other hand, even though the game is incredibly fun, I would really like it to be a bit more realistic in its mechanics and physics so that the horror immersion can be complete.

Despite these balance issues, I am thrilled that the major change to the graphics engine and animations has finally been officially confirmed. Knowing they are going to give a massive overhaul to the models, lighting, and atmosphere gives me a lot of hope for the future of the game. I hope that along with this huge visual upgrade, they also bring the gameplay fixes that the community is asking for so much.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe severe matchmaking imbalances that pit newer players against opponents with thousands of hours.

citations.review_text:
Dead by Daylight has a brilliant core idea. The concept of one killer hunting four survivors is still one of the most interesting multiplayer ideas out there. The first 20-50 hours are genuinely fun. You get to try different killers and survivors, experiment with perks, learn the maps, and it feels like the game has a lot of depth.

Around the 100-hour mark, you start realizing that the biggest problem with this game is how badly balanced it is.

The matchmaking is one of the worst parts. A player with 100 hours can easily end up against people with 10000-15000 hours. Thats not an exaggeration. That kind of experience gap makes many matches feel decided before they even start.

The maps are another major problem. Some of them are incredibly survivor-sided, especially if youre playing an M1 killer. In many matches youre fighting the map design more than the survivors themselves.

The biggest imbalance is SWF. A coordinated four-man group on voice chat has a massive advantage in communication and information. At that point DBD stops feeling like one killer versus four survivors. It feels like four survivors having fun at one killers expense.

Cheaters are another serious issue. One survivor using cheats is enough to ruin the entire match. The worst part is that the game regularly sends notifications saying action has been taken against players I previously played with. That means this isnt some rare one-off problem.

What disappoints me the most is the developers priorities. New skins, collections, and paid cosmetics keep coming out constantly, but the problems with maps, matchmaking, SWF balance, and older killers have existed for years. It feels like the monetization side of the game gets far more attention than the core gameplay issues.

I dont regret spending almost 300 hours in DBD. The atmosphere is great, the perk variety is fun, and the core concept is genuinely unique. But this is a game that makes an excellent first impression and a very poor l…

This game is genuinely one of the worst things I've ever had the misfortune of playing, I originally started playing in 2017. I was a young little minded jitt and i thought then, man this game is ♥♥♥♥! claims.claim: Reviewers note that the in-game tutorial is poor, forcing new players to rely on external sources to learn how to play.

citations.review_text:
A game that is both addicting and miserable at the same time. What should be a fun, casual party game at its core has devolved into a competitive, toxic mess.

Playing as Killer – Miserable

If you're new to the game and want to play Killer, prepare for one of the most insufferable learning experiences imaginable. It's like showing up to school with no pants on and having to stand infront of the class. You'll be tbagged, blinded, moonwalked on, and watch three generators pop in front of your face while four survivors make sure you know exactly how bad you are.

Want to play as one of your favourite horror icons? Too bad. Most of them are locked behind paid DLC with no real workaround. Some of the strongest perks are also locked behind owning specific killers unless you're willing to wait and pray they appear in the Shrine.

Eventually, after dozens of painful matches, you might finally feel confident enough to play Killer. Then matchmaking decides it's time to introduce you to a coordinated four-man bully squad whose sole objective is to make your game is long and painful. At that point, you start questioning who the real killer is, because it sure as hell isn't you.

Playing as Survivor – Also Miserable

Unless you have three friends willing to queue with you, prepare to rely on random teammates who seem determined to lose the game.

You'll get teammates who body-block you, sandbag you, rat in corners, or spend the entire match acting like they're the main character. The worst part is they often play with massive egos despite making some of the worst decisions imaginable. Every match feels like you're fighting a losing battle while dragging your own team across the finish line or hanging on your final hook watching your team decide what they are gonna eat that night.

Overall, it's another exhausting experience.

The Game itself is buggy, poorly balanced, and often more frustrating than fun. BHVR continues to prioritise graphic updates, cosmetic collaborations, and…

I've played a lot of this game, and had plenty of fun with it, but I cannot recommend this game if you are a new player, it is incredibly hard to learn, you'll have to rely on otz and hens as the tutorial is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the community is the single most toxic community on the internet. You will receive death threats, slurs, personal attacks, tbagging at the gate, face camping, etc. Additionally, this is one of the ONLY online games that doesn't have dedicated servers, if your killer is lagging, so will you, and whatever happens on the killer's screen goes regardless of what happened on yours, meaning you get hit on some ridiculous vaults or get those hits when the survivor is long gone. Behaviour also seemingly care very little about balancing, as there are a few killers in the game exponentially stronger than the others, they did FINALLY nerf blight, but nurse (and Jason imo) are still egregious examples of bad game design. But if you are a killer main and want to be even remotely ethical, and play a weaker killer, or just so happens your favourite killer is a weaker one, there will be many games that you lose, that you simply never had a chance of winning, whether its a bad map for the killer, the survivors were coordinated and simply leave with no effort, or you get out-perked. Speaking of perks, there are a few perks on both sides of the game that are just so much better than the other perks, you never have a reason to use them, some of these perks do the same thing as another perk, but just better.
I tend to go on several month long breaks from the game because it just gets too miserable to play, occasionally coming back for new content. I really would like to recommend this game, but in its current state, I can't.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a steep learning curve and a vast, overwhelming number of perks to learn.

citations.review_text:
So, if i have 1000 hours at the time of this negative review, it can't be that bad right? Well unfortunately, the one thing this game has over its competition, is that it doesn't have any competition. So if the asymmetrical genre is to your fancy, unfortunately you just don't have any other options to scratch the itch of scary guy chase little guy.

Fun concept and general execution. If you know what you're doing, you're gonna have a blast, but this game has a steep learning curve and a clinical imbalance at almost all times. As of right now, while casual lobbies can swing either way, there is a massive amount of power creep towards the above average player playing in a squad of friends (colloquially known as SWYFs). The balance Behavior Interactive has leaned in favor of, is catering to new or casual players who don't know how to play the game very well, with many of the game's perks allowing you to give yourself a "second chance" in situations that don't feel earned and/or counterintuitive (classically, many unbalanced perks are earned in a way that punishes the other role for playing their side of the gameplay loop as intended). However when the same perks are used by competent players, they become unbalanced in a way that can make you genuinely feel like the developer is endorsing a form of exploit abuse. Sometimes, experiencing blatant cheaters can be a more engaging experience, and yes, cheat/hacked client users are also regularly rampant in this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that cheaters are a serious issue in matches.

citations.review_text:
Dead by Daylight has a brilliant core idea. The concept of one killer hunting four survivors is still one of the most interesting multiplayer ideas out there. The first 20-50 hours are genuinely fun. You get to try different killers and survivors, experiment with perks, learn the maps, and it feels like the game has a lot of depth.

Around the 100-hour mark, you start realizing that the biggest problem with this game is how badly balanced it is.

The matchmaking is one of the worst parts. A player with 100 hours can easily end up against people with 10000-15000 hours. Thats not an exaggeration. That kind of experience gap makes many matches feel decided before they even start.

The maps are another major problem. Some of them are incredibly survivor-sided, especially if youre playing an M1 killer. In many matches youre fighting the map design more than the survivors themselves.

The biggest imbalance is SWF. A coordinated four-man group on voice chat has a massive advantage in communication and information. At that point DBD stops feeling like one killer versus four survivors. It feels like four survivors having fun at one killers expense.

Cheaters are another serious issue. One survivor using cheats is enough to ruin the entire match. The worst part is that the game regularly sends notifications saying action has been taken against players I previously played with. That means this isnt some rare one-off problem.

What disappoints me the most is the developers priorities. New skins, collections, and paid cosmetics keep coming out constantly, but the problems with maps, matchmaking, SWF balance, and older killers have existed for years. It feels like the monetization side of the game gets far more attention than the core gameplay issues.

I dont regret spending almost 300 hours in DBD. The atmosphere is great, the perk variety is fun, and the core concept is genuinely unique. But this is a game that makes an excellent first impression and a very poor l…
